definition: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a sub-field of reinforcement learning.
details: It focuses on studying the behavior of multiple learning agents that coexist in a shared environment. Each agent is motivated by its own rewards, and does actions to advance its own interests; in some environments these interests are opposed to the interests of other agents, resulting in complex group dynamics. Multi-agent reinforcement learning is closely related to game theory and especially repeated games, as well as multi-agent systems. Its study combines the pursuit of finding ideal algorithms that maximize rewards with a more sociological set of concepts. While research in single-agent reinforcement learning is concerned with finding the algorithm that gets the biggest number of points for one agent, research in multi-agent reinforcement learning evaluates and quantifies social metrics, such as cooperation, reciprocity, equity, social influence, language and discrimination.

explainer.lead: MARL studies multiple learning agents sharing one environment, each pursuing its own reward. It matters because group dynamics and opposing interests make learning far harder than single-agent RL and connect it to game theory.

tiers.eli5: Imagine several players in one game, each trying to win for themselves while seeing everyone else's moves. Each learns how to play better, but because others keep changing too, the game never stands still.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use MARL when several agents must act in one shared environment, often framing it as a repeated game. A common pitfall is that one agent's learning changes the environment for the others, so training can be unstable.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, n agents each choose actions in a shared environment and receive their own rewards; the problem relates to repeated games and multi-agent systems. Known limit: with opposed interests the dynamics are complex and ideal algorithms are only pursued, not guaranteed.

explainer.example: Two competing agents in a shared market each adjust strategy from their own rewards, and each one's shift alters what the other faces.
